A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Selective Prompt Anchoring by the same authors. All 25 pages of v3.pdf and 24 pages of v5.pdf, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support comparison. Relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v3.pdf reports original benchmark evaluations, attention analyses, ablations, tuning experiments and inference-time measurements in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v5.pdf retains these original experiments and adds LiveCodeBench results, difficulty-stratified code-length comparisons and a fixed-strength SPA evaluation.

M1.justification: The masking operation, logit combination in Equation 14, test-failure activation and Appendix F beam-search procedure remain unchanged. The fixed-strength experiment evaluates an existing hyperparameter choice. Parallelization and top-logit truncation are discussed as possible optimizations, without establishing changes to the implemented method.

E1.justification: v5 adds the 1,055-task LiveCodeBench release, extending coverage to recent competitive-programming tasks. Existing HumanEval, MBPP, BigCodeBench, multilingual and non-code task coverage remains. This is a bounded extension of the existing code-generation evaluation.

E2.justification: The external comparators remain PASTA, Self-Debugging, Self-Edit, Self-Planning and ReAct, with the existing comparisons retained. v5 Table 13 additionally compares tuned SPA against SPA-fixed-strength, an internal comparison variant rather than a new external baseline.

E3.justification: v5 introduces comparisons within LiveCodeBench's easy, medium and hard groups and evaluates a fixed anchoring strength obtained by averaging tuned strengths across benchmarks for each model. Existing five-fold tuning and decoding protocols remain. The explicit temperature, beam-size and zero-shot statements in Appendix H are additional disclosures, not demonstrated protocol revisions.

E4.justification: v5 adds a difficulty-stratified check of the relationship between generation length and correctness, a fixed-strength tuning analysis, and LiveCodeBench anchor-selection ablations. Existing prompt-length, transferability, beam-search, no-test-case and code-example analyses remain. The anchoring-strength analysis in Section 5.6 was already present in v3 Appendix J.1.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same five-fold procedure, five-subset tuning analysis and anchoring-strength variances of 0.0046 and 0.0026. Neither introduces new seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: v5 adds LiveCodeBench scores, including 11.9% base versus 15.8% SPA Pass@1 for DeepSeek-Coder-33B, difficulty-specific length means, fixed-strength SPA's +5.0-point result, and a 0.1-second average test-execution time. Existing benchmark scores largely match. CodeLlama's BigCodeBench relative gain changes from 5% in v3 Table 14 to 21% in v5 Table 17, although v5 Table 2 still reports 5%.

T1.justification: The attention equations and Taylor/finite-difference derivation remain substantively unchanged. Appendix E.2 adds a formal memory-cost expression, M_overhead = V × D × S_logit, and worked memory estimates, replacing v3's purely qualitative memory-overhead statement.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: identifying attention dilution, proposing model-agnostic and training-free SPA, and reporting improvements up to 12.9% in Pass@1. The additional experiments support these retained claims without materially redefining them.

C2.justification: Section 7 adds an explicit limitation concerning benchmark-test-based activation and proposes generated tests and error-guided reuse of SPA. It expands existing dynamic-anchoring ideas while removing discussion of unexplained relationships with model attributes and possible RNN adaptation. New passages also discuss attention misalignment, fixed-strength deployment and memory–latency tradeoffs.

D1.justification: Appendix H adds Transformers generation-API and hook details, access information for the anchoring PyPI package, explicit zero-shot prompting, and temperature 0/beam 1 settings except for Appendix F. Appendix E newly states that logits are computed sequentially. The earlier KV-cache/FlashAttention implementation statement disappears, without establishing that those optimizations were disabled. Hardware and quantization disclosures remain.

R1.justification: v5 adds LiveCodeBench, interactive code/SQL-generation work and attention-pattern/misalignment studies to its positioning. It removes the FlashAttention and Scissorhands references and drops the explicit contrast that SPA, unlike PASTA, avoids manual user input. The principal related-work categories and novelty positioning remain.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and section order remain, with localized rewrites of method explanations, related work, limitations and computational costs. v5 merges the earlier gradient-attention material into Appendix B, moves Appendix M to A, promotes Appendix J.1 to Section 5.6, and subdivides Appendices E and H. Conference front matter, acknowledgements and an impact statement are added.

P2.justification: v5 substantially changes visual organization through a two-column main paper and references, resized and relocated displays, and revised table widths. It replaces the main pooled-length boxplot with a difficulty table while retaining the boxplots in Appendix A, adds LiveCodeBench columns and a fixed-strength comparison table, and moves the anchoring-strength plot into the main text.

improvement.justification: v5 modestly strengthens empirical support and usability through LiveCodeBench results, a difficulty-stratified check beyond v3's pooled length comparison, fixed-strength evaluation and concrete implementation/package information. The length analysis remains observational. The new memory estimate in Appendix E.2 contains an unexplained embedding-dimension factor, and the CodeLlama percentage correction is inconsistent across Tables 2 and 17. These weaknesses limit the gains from the added validation and documentation.
